questions.q: In this capstone's scenario, what is the very first thing you do with a new, unfamiliar ServiceNow instance?
options: Start making configuration changes immediately
Explore the Application Navigator to figure out what the instance actually is before changing anything
Delete any tables you don't recognize
Assume it's identical to every other ServiceNow instance you've seen
questions.explain: A new admin's first job is reconnaissance: understand what's actually installed and in use before touching configuration.

questions.q: Typing "tables" into the Application Navigator filter on Meridian Freight's instance surfaces which view?
options: System Applications > Store
System Definition > Tables, the list of every table in the instance
The Service Catalog item list
The user's personal profile page
questions.explain: System Definition > Tables lists every table (the sys_db_object table) and is the fastest way to see what an instance is built to track.

questions.q: Why does finding the cmdb_ci table on this instance matter, specifically?
options: It has no particular significance
It only matters for HR-related applications
It confirms the instance has a Configuration Item base to extend from, which any asset/configuration management setup needs
It means the instance cannot have an Incident table
questions.explain: cmdb_ci is the base table any CI subtype (servers, routers, etc.) extends from, so finding it confirms a normal CMDB foundation.

questions.q: Why isn't finding a table in the schema enough to prove an application is actively used?
options: ServiceNow ships a large standard table structure regardless of whether the matching application is actually turned on and used
Tables are deleted the moment an application is uninstalled
It actually is enough — no further check is needed
Tables only appear after an application has processed real records
questions.explain: A table's existence reflects the base schema, not whether that application is installed and populated with real records — those require a separate check.

questions.q: Which four ITSM modules does this lesson expect to find installed and populated on Meridian Freight's instance?
options: HR Case, Benefits, Payroll, and Onboarding
GL, AP, AR, and Subledger Accounting
Incident, Problem, Change, and Request
Flow Designer, Script Includes, Business Rules, and ACLs
questions.explain: These are the core service-desk ITSM modules from Course 1's hands-on practices, and the ones a logistics company's service desk would run day to day.
